claim: SQLite assumes by default that a sector write is not atomic.
quote: SQLite has traditionally assumed that a sector write is not atomic.

claim: Changes to data files may be written only after the WAL records describing them have been flushed to permanent storage.
quote: changes to data files (where tables and indexes reside) must be written only after those changes have been logged, that is, after WAL records describing the changes have been flushed to permanent storage.

claim: After a crash, changes not yet applied to data pages are redone from the WAL records.
quote: any changes that have not been applied to the data pages can be redone from the WAL records. (This is roll-forward recovery, also known as REDO.)

claim: The WAL is written sequentially, so syncing it costs much less than flushing data pages.
quote: The WAL file is written sequentially, and so the cost of syncing the WAL is much less than the cost of flushing the data pages.

claim: With many small concurrent transactions, one fsync of the WAL can commit many of them.
quote: when the server is processing many small concurrent transactions, one fsync of the WAL file may suffice to commit many transactions.

claim: fsync blocks until the device reports that the transfer of the file's modified data has completed.
quote: The call blocks until the device reports that the transfer has completed.
